Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Karl Feller 
Okeana, OH 45053

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Janet Zimmerman 
Pine Island, NY 10969

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Simona Vigil

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Larissa Matthews 
Plainview, NY 11803

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 mark kottenbrock 
bismarck, ND 58501

protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Elizabeth Cano 
Miami, FL 33174

agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Nancy Anne Earl 
San Francisco, CA 94131

farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Leora Yoak 
Conway, AR 72034

 
 
 
Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Carl and Mary Melin 
Buena Park, CA 90620

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Alex Vishio 
Baltimore, MD 21239

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Gail Brooks 
Los Osos, CA 93402

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Debbie Kaufman 
Wellington, FL 33414

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Cindy Hatcher 
Bumpus Mills, TN 37028

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Andreas Rossing Angeltveit 
,  3915

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Cs Royce 
Danbury, CT 6810

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Sonya Grant 
Akron, OH 44305

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Dorothy Chamberlin 
Colorado Springs, CO 80905

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free

protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Carol Drake 
Fremont, CA 94536

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Tracy Anderson 
Eagan, MN 55123

protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Susan McKenzie 
Meadow Vista, CA 95722

agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Madalina Bercaru-Maxim 
Plano, TX 75025

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Brett Stahl 
Dallas, TX 75248

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Greg Lowe 
Davie, FL 33325

catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 John Crombie 
, IN 47136

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Iris Rochkind 
East Elmhurst, NY 11370

protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jörg Gaiser 
Baiersbronn,  72270

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 K. M. 
, MI 48002

farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Robert Lipsky 
Kensington, MD 20895

 
 
 
Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jennifer Eastley 
Charlestown, NH 3603

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Arthur Hoyt 
, AR 72654

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Barbara Hall 
San Mateo, CA 94403

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Emma Houseman 
Chelmsford, MA 1824

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Robert Nunez

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Sandy Holder 
Eugene, OR 97404

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Yonit Yogev 
Olympia, WA 98502

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Wayne Whitaker 
, GA 30033

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Kimberly Vincent 
Sandy, UT 84093

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 liza mai 
Berlin, AK 99501

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Yi-Mei Lu

catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Phyllis Lager 
Livermore, CA 94550

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Alice Rim 
Buford, GA 30518

the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Suzanne Jacobs 
, FL 33437

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Rod Storey 
Schenectady, NY 12345

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Ramji Patel 
, MI 48152

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Carol Masuda 
Evanston, IL 60202

health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Karen Cotterell 
New York, NY 10012

farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Ken Sharp 
Marmora, NJ 8223

 
 
 
Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Linda Roberts 
Burr Ridge, IL 60527

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Cyril Bouteille 
Mountain View, CA 94040

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Byron Fogel 
Van Nuys, CA 91402

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Barbara Clewett 
Lexington, KY 40517

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate.

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Elizabeth Nugen 
Friendship, WI 53934

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Stephen Henry 
Berkeley, CA 94705

protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Richard Sawyer 
Warwick, MD 21912

agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Karen Stimson 
Orange, CT 6477

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Amy Whitworth 
Portland, OR 97214
