Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Elizabeth Adan

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 James Hildebrand 
Mobile, AL 36602

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Diedre Bollinger 
Stephentown, NY 12168

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Peter Reilly 
Redford, MI 48240

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jenn Cunningham 
Manchester, NH 3103

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Alison Zyla 
Clinton, CT 6413

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Luis Lozano 
Long Beach, CA 90803

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Katie Brady 
Carson City, NV 89703

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Robert Linzmeier 
Palatine, IL 60074

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Laurie Swenson 
Bend, OR 97702

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Judith Robinson 
Matawan, NJ 7747

Dear Scott Pruitt,

agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Melinda Fritsch 
Aransas Pass, TX 78336

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Frank Wyse 
Mesa, AZ 85209

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Marie Maciel 
Bridgewater, NJ 8807

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Susan Johnson 
MC DADE, TX 78650

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Laura Lyons 
Ludington, MI 49431

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free

protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Joan Angelosanto 
Melrose, MA 2176

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 William Klock 
Watauga, TX 76148

protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jeanne Davenport 
Long Beach, CA 90808

agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 R Kenneth Reece 
Knoxville, TN 37922

farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Gerolynn Laukevicz 
New Milford, CT 6776

 
 
 
Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Noam Eisen 
Pittsburgh, PA 15208

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Julienne Travers 
St.Joseph, MO 64501

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Gloria Lee 
San Francisco, CA 94122

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Chloé Mekinc 
Glenmoore, PA 19343

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Mark Heald 
Pleasant Hill, TN 38578

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Kalyn Behnke 
Fountain Hills, AZ 85268

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Patricia Aubin 
Plattsburgh, NY 12901

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Martina Capannini 
, ot 50127

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Greg Cover 
Oakland, CA 94611

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Bonnie McLean 
Pensacola, FL 32503

catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Kathy Kestell 
Spokane, WA 99208

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Germain Giner 
, IL 60640

the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Christy Fisher 
Eureka, CA 95503

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Susan Zimmer 
Leland, NC 28451

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Sarah Harvey 
Oakland, CA 94606

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Steven Christian 
Hillsboro, OR 97123

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Steve Massey 
,  0

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Richard Hingel 
San Francisco, CA 94115

 
 
 
Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Susan Arkin 
Jamaica, NY 11432

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Gerald Ryan 
Flemington, NJ 8822

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Rosellen Sell 
, CO 80501

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Maureen Mehler 
Laguna Woods, CT 92637

health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Bailey Bear 
Minneapolis, MN 55423

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Marilise Tronto 
New York, NY 10034

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Lee Steinmetz

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 matt cutts 
greeneville, TN 37743

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Virginia Smith 
Washington, PA 15301

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Colleen Sheahon 
Boone, NC 28607

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Thomas Durst 
Ashland, OR 97520

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Nick Heath 
Boston, MA 2116

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Maria Nesheim 
Aptos, CA 95003

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Frank De Haan 
Sun Valley, CA 91352

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Timothy Bruck 
Mentor, OH 44060
