protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Marilyn Barthelow 
Auburn, CA 95602

health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Louise Berliner 
concord, MA 1742

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Ray Rodney 
Woodacre, CA 94973

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Robert Derman

catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Osiel Bonfim 
Portland, OR 97202

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Erin Gellman 
redway, CA 95560

the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Valerie Majercsik 
Johnstown, PA 15905

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Patricia Nicholoff 
, WA 98020

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jerome Rickert 
Hinsdale, IL 60521

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jean Pauley 
Seattle, WA 98112

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Stephen Bauser 
Chicago, IL 60605

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Melody Nielsen 
, WY 82007

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Bracha N. Bomze 
NY, NY 10024

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Joanne Harenburg 
Phoenix, AZ 85034

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Susan Clark 
Duluth, MN 55811

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Lou Hasenwinkel 
Spirit lake, IA 51360

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 J.T. Smith 
Sellersville, PA 18960

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Steffani Aarons 
NEW YORK, NY 10003

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Bruce Waterman 
Oakland, CA 94609

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Virgil Pauls 
Newton, KS 67114

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 John Hewett 
Playa del Rey, CA 90293

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Nicole Best 
Clearfield, UT 84015

Dear Scott Pruitt,

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Roger Anker 
Matteson, IL 60443

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Bill King 
McHenry, IL 60051

take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Aaron Koch 
Great Mills, MD 20634

agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Wesley Wolf 
Lake Barrington, IL 60010

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 jill donovan

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 James Rego 
Fairfield, CA 94534

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Sandra Brouillette-Jobe 
Freeland, WA 98249

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 David Greene 
North Huntingdon,, PA 15642

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Mark Fabian 
Pittsburgh, PA 15227

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Sandra Davidson 
Titusville, FL 32796

protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jamie Marchi 
Chicago, IL 60631

health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Marjorie Wing 
Lansing, MI 48911

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Jason Barthe 
BEAVERTON, OR 97008

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Lauren Ruiz 
Concord, NH 3301

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Judith Elzinga 
Glenwood springs`, CO 81601

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Steven Pautz 
Ardmore, AL 35739

protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jeannie Pollak 
oxnard, CA 93036

agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Susan Fraser 
Carrollton, TX 75010

farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Catherine Gauthier 
San Diego, CA 94602

 
 
 
Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Denise Schmidt 
Dillon, CO 80435

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Michelle Skinner 
Guerneville, CA 95446

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Corey Mac 
South Bend, IN 46619

the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 James Walters 
Lake Lure, NC 28746

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Steve Troyanovich 
Florence, NJ 8518

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Shannon Wileman 
Anchorage, AK 99516

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Arthur Krakowsky 
Livermore, CA 94550

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 H.H.C. Krug 
Waterloo, ON 0

the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Shirley Love

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Harry Hochheiser 
Pittsburgh, PA 15217

farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Faye Soares 
Pollock Pines, CA 95726

 
 
 
Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Amy Wolfe 
Scottsdale, AZ 85251

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Suzanne Phillips 
Orleans, MA 2653

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Denise Pretet 
New Lenox, IL 60451

contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Thomas Driscoll 
San Rafael, CA 94901

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union
