Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jon DeLong 
Half Moon Bay, CA 94019

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Vivian Sovran 
Seattle, WA 98107

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Ziona Schulthess

health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Deborah Cudworth 
New Hope, PA 18938

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Megan DeSantis 
Woodinville, WA 98072

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Susan Green 
Avon, CT 6001

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Shela Hadley 
Cambridge, MA 2138

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Eric Lehmann 
Santa Barbara, CA 93101

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 J Woodhull

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jennifer Bradley 
santa monica, CA 90404

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 dick hogle 
Espanola, NM 87532

the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Marc Dumas 
Fairbanks, AK 99712

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA

Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Karen Shovein 
Taylor, MI 48180

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Gina Bates 
Apple Creek, OH 44606

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Jennifer Carter

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Dave Heilemann 
Pahoa, HI 96778

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 John Sharrer 
Pahoa, HI 96778

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Louise Rickard 
Lincoln, VT 5443

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Eric Andersen 
Kaukauna, WI 54130

take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Neilia Pierson 
Cave Junction, OR 97523

agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Paul Augustine 
, OR 97707

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Lyle Eklof 
SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, CA 94080

 
 
 
Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Donald Williams 
Somerville, MA 2144

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 L Michetti 
Fort Lee, NJ 7024

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 JoAnne Larsen 
Lee, MA 1238

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Candace Davis 
Seattle, WA 98105

health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Rebecca Cook 
Friday Harbor, WA 98250

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Ruth MacLean

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Michael Sawicky 
, OR 97520

catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Martha Potter Kim 
Falmouth,, MA 2540

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Carole Kruse 
Troy, NY 12182

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Carol Barbee 
Florence, OR 97439

have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Lanna Ultican 
Blue Springs, MO 64015

farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Mike Esqueda 
La Puente, CA 91744

 
 
 
Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Sandy Bushberg 
Hood River, OR 97031

the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Cindy Borske 
Mason City, IA 50659

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Sandra Lambert 
Mansfield Center, CT 6250

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Sandra Nelson 
Rancho Mirage, CA 92270

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 John Boltz

are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Mary Bobb 
Miami, FL 33150

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Ronald Paige MSG USA Ret 
Lansing, MI 48911

license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 michael waters 
sedona, AZ 86336

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Lorraine Price 
jackson, TN 38305

impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

 Samuel Grossinger 
Durham, NC 27712

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment.

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Agnieszka Beletsky 
East New Market, MD 21631

Subject: Pesticide rules 

Dear Scott Pruitt, 

I am writing to you to urge you to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations to protect public 
health and the environment. Countries around the world are restricting the most dangerous 
agricultural chemicals, and the United States is falling behind. Canada and the European Union 
have partial bans on neonicotinoids, and the European Union has a partial ban on glyphosate. 
Chlorpyrifos and atrazine are restricted in the European Union. We know that these pesticides 
are killing pollinators and polluting our environment while threatening our health. It is time we 
catch up.  

The United States should not prioritize corporate profit over the protection of public health and 
the environment. Pesticide companies are looking for the Trump administration to give them free 
license to continue polluting at unsustainable and dangerous levels. The job of the EPA is to 
protect the public and our environment from harmful chemicals. To that end, I request that EPA 
take action to strengthen, not weaken, pesticide regulations.  

I am concerned that the new administration is favoring corporate interests over the interests of 
the public due to conflicts of interest. For example, Dow, the manufacturer of chlorpyrifos, 
contributed $1 million to Donald Trump’s inaugural committee. This neurotoxic pesticide's 
impending restriction by EPA, based on strong science demonstrating harm to children and 
farmworkers, was recently reversed by EPA. We’ve seen similar conflicts of interest occur in 
review of other chemicals. I urge EPA to consider the communities whose health is at risk due to 
insufficient protection against pesticides when constructing new rules, and not give in to pressure 
from pesticide companies at the expense of our health and environment. 

Sincerely, 
 Linda Ondo 
Stevenson Ranch, CA 91381
